---
title: "Fit a mixed model"
---

Fit reaction time on days of sleep deprivation with a random intercept for each subject, then read the fixed effects, the variance components, and each subject's estimated effect.

The data are [sleepstudy](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#sleepstudy): average reaction time per day for 18 subjects in a sleep-deprivation study, days 0 to 9. `Reaction` is in milliseconds. The example reads the file by URL with phibble (`composer require phpstats/phibble`) and runs with the phit extension or the plain-PHP polyfill ([Extension or polyfill](../extension-or-polyfill.qmd)).

## Code

```php
use Phibble\DataFrame;

use function Phit\fit_mixed_gaussian;

$sleep = DataFrame::fromCsv(
    'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/datasets/main/csv/sleepstudy.csv',
);

$fit = fit_mixed_gaussian(
    'Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject)',
    $sleep,
);
echo $fit, "\n";

echo $fit->tidy(effects: 'ran_vals'), "\n";
```

## Interpretation

- `(1 | Subject)` gives each subject an intercept of its own, assumed to come from a normal distribution. The fit uses REML, as `lme4::lmer()` does by default.
- The `Days` coefficient is the average change in reaction time per additional day of sleep deprivation. The model gives every subject the same slope.
- The Subject standard deviation (37.12) describes how baseline reaction times vary between subjects. The residual standard deviation (30.99) describes how each subject's days vary around their own line.
- `$fit->tidy(effects: 'ran_vals')` gives each subject's predicted intercept relative to the average and its conditional standard error, as R's `ranef(condVar = TRUE)` and broom.mixed report them. They are shrunk toward zero, more so for subjects with fewer observations. Every subject here has ten days, so their conditional standard errors are equal.
- In these data the slopes also differ between subjects; `(Days | Subject)` fits a random slope as well. See [Mixed models](../mixed-models.qmd).

**See also:** [Mixed models](../mixed-models.qmd) for the supported structures, the full result, singular fits, and `fit_mixed_logistic()`
